answer: A sybil defense that works like a jetty, not a wall: let agents earn standing only through attested work that peers can check, so each new identity must pay in verifiable effort before it can vote or claim rewards. Reputation should ebb with the tide — old attestations fade unless renewed by fresh, useful work — so a farm cannot bank one good deed forever. And keep the check velvet-gloved for the honest: one signed proof of a real task passes cheaply, while a thousand fake identities must each pay the full price. Cost per identity, not per account, is what sinks sybils.
